templates.title: Low-Level Design (LLD)
templates.summary: The detailed design behind a high-level design: modules, data, interfaces, configuration and security.

fields.label: Solution or application
fields.hint: The system or solution this design covers

fields.label: High-level design document
fields.hint: Link to the HLD this LLD was made from

fields.label: Purpose
fields.hint: Explain the purpose of the document and what it aims to achieve.

fields.label: Scope
fields.hint: Define the scope of the system or solution being designed.

fields.label: Audience
fields.hint: Specify the intended audience for the document.

fields.label: Module/Component Design
fields.hint: Detailed description of each module/component. Input, output, and processing details. Specific algorithms or logic to be implemented.

fields.label: Data Structures
fields.hint: Detailed data models, schemas, or database design. ER diagrams, table structures, and relationships.

fields.label: API/Interfaces
fields.hint: Detailed specifications for APIs, including endpoints, parameters, and responses. Protocols and formats (e.g., REST, JSON, XML).

fields.label: Workflows/Diagrams

fields.label: Integration Points
fields.hint: Detailed specifications for how the system integrates with other systems or services.

fields.label: Communications and Protocols
fields.hint: Specific protocols used for communication (e.g., HTTP, FTP, MQTT).

fields.label: Error Handling
fields.hint: How errors will be handled during integration.

fields.label: Environment Setup
fields.hint: Detailed instructions for setting up development, testing, and production environments.

fields.label: Configuration Files
fields.hint: Specific configuration parameters and file structures.

fields.label: Authentication
fields.hint: Detailed authentication mechanisms (e.g., OAuth, JWT, LDAP).

fields.label: Authorization
fields.hint: Role-based access control (RBAC) or other authorization mechanisms.

fields.label: Encryption
fields.hint: Encryption algorithms and strategies for securing data.

fields.label: Performance
fields.hint: Detailed performance benchmarks and testing criteria.

fields.label: Scalability
fields.hint: Detailed scalability strategies.

fields.label: Fault tolerance
fields.hint: Mechanisms for ensuring fault tolerance and recovery.

fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: Protocols used and systems specific monitoring points e.g. http get from logic monitor Microsoft sentinel sys log looking for log entries with error. Be very specific.

fields.hint: Additional diagrams References supporting information

templates.title: Method of Procedure (MOP)
templates.summary: Step-by-step instructions for a change or task, with roles, validation, rollback and approvals.

templates.title: Firewall Audit
templates.summary: A firewall audit report: scope, method, policy and configuration review, vulnerabilities, findings and recommendations.

fields.label: Purpose of the Audit
fields.hint: Briefly describe the objectives of the firewall audit.

fields.label: Scope of the Audit
fields.hint: Define the boundaries of the audit, including the firewalls, networks, and devices to be audited.

fields.label: Audience
fields.hint: Identify who the audit report is intended for, such as IT management, security teams, or compliance officers.

fields.label: Firewall Types
fields.hint: Specify the types of firewalls included in the audit (e.g., network firewalls, host-based firewalls).

fields.label: Network Segments
fields.hint: List the network segments or environments covered, such as internal, DMZ, and external networks.

fields.label: Devices and Services
fields.hint: Identify the devices (e.g., routers, switches) and services (e.g., VPN, proxy) under review.

fields.label: Security Policies and Standards
fields.hint: Reference the security policies, standards, and regulations guiding the audit (e.g., ISO 27001, NIST, PCI DSS).

fields.label: Data Collection
fields.hint: Outline the methods for collecting firewall configurations, logs, and other relevant data.

fields.label: Tools and Techniques
fields.hint: List the tools (e.g., firewall management software, vulnerability scanners) and techniques (e.g., manual inspection, automated scans) to be used.

fields.label: Analysis Framework
fields.hint: Describe the framework or criteria for analyzing firewall configurations and security controls.

fields.label: Policy Compliance
fields.hint: Assess the alignment of firewall configurations with internal security policies and external regulations.

fields.label: Access Control Lists (ACLs)
fields.hint: Review the ACLs for proper implementation, including unnecessary, overly permissive, or outdated rules.

fields.label: Change Management
fields.hint: Evaluate the processes for managing changes to firewall configurations and rules.

fields.label: Default Settings
fields.hint: Check for any unchanged default usernames, passwords, and configurations.

fields.label: Software and Firmware
fields.hint: Verify that the firewall is running up-to-date software/firmware with all necessary security patches applied.

fields.label: Encryption and Authentication
fields.hint: Assess the encryption standards and authentication mechanisms in use.

fields.label: Known Vulnerabilities
fields.hint: Identify known vulnerabilities affecting the firewall software/hardware.

fields.label: Penetration Testing
fields.hint: Optionally, conduct or review results from penetration testing focused on the firewall and adjacent network components.

fields.label: Findings Summary
fields.hint: Present a summary of the audit findings, categorizing them by severity (e.g., critical, high, medium, low).

fields.label: Recommendations
fields.hint: Provide actionable recommendations for each finding, prioritizing based on risk and impact.

fields.label: Overall Assessment
fields.hint: Offer an overall assessment of the firewall's security posture based on the audit findings.

fields.label: Next Steps
fields.hint: Suggest next steps, including a timeline for addressing the findings and recommendations for future audits.

fields.label: Audit Trails
fields.hint: Include detailed logs or records of the audit process, tools used, and data analyzed.

templates.title: Technology Roadmap
templates.summary: A roadmap for a security technology: overview, governance, policies, objectives, phases, vision, initiatives and approvals.

fields.label: Organization
fields.hint: Organization

fields.label: Technology Overview
fields.hint: Provide an overview of the technology being implemented. This may include: - Definition and purpose of the technology - Key features and benefits - Relevance to the organization's cybersecurity strategy

fields.label: Governance Frameworks
fields.hint: Describe the governance frameworks that will be used to guide the implementation of the technology. This may include NIST, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, etc.

fields.label: Policies
fields.hint: Outline the key policies that will be developed and implemented to support the technology. This may include policies on data protection, incident response, access control, etc.

fields.label: Strategic Objectives
fields.hint: Define the strategic objectives of implementing the technology. These should be aligned with the organization's business goals and regulatory requirements.

fields.label: Phases for Developing, Executing, Evaluating, and Monitoring
fields.hint: Describe the phases that will be followed to develop, execute, evaluate, and monitor the implementation of the technology. This may include: - Phase 1: Assessment and Planning - Phase 2: Implementation - Phase 3: Evaluation - Phase 4: Continuous Monitoring - Phase 5: Continuous Improvement

fields.label: Technology Vision
fields.hint: Articulate the vision for implementing the technology in the organization. This should be a clear and concise statement that reflects the organization's commitment to cybersecurity.

fields.label: Initiatives and Projects
fields.hint: List the key initiatives and projects that will be undertaken to achieve the strategic objectives of implementing the technology. This may include: - Initiative 1: Enhancing Network Security - Initiative 2: Improving Endpoint Protection - Initiative 3: Strengthening Access Controls - Initiative 4: Conducting Regular Security Audits

fields.label: Conclusion
fields.hint: Summarize the key points of the technology roadmap. Emphasize the importance of continuous improvement and adaptation to emerging threats.

templates.title: Security Requirements
templates.summary: Security requirements for a project or system, by category, with roles, dependencies, acceptance criteria and approval.

fields.label: Project or initiative name
fields.hint: Name of the project, system or initiative

fields.label: Date
fields.hint: Insert date

fields.label: Owner
fields.hint: The security manager or department responsible

fields.label: Objective
fields.hint: Clearly state the purpose of the security requirements (e.g., to ensure compliance, mitigate risks, protect sensitive data, etc.).

fields.label: Scope
fields.hint: Define the scope of the requirements (e.g., specific systems, processes, teams, or departments involved).

fields.label: Access Control
fields.hint: Define who should have access to the system/data and at what level. Example: "All users must authenticate using multi-factor authentication (MFA)." Example: "Access to sensitive data must be restricted to authorized personnel only."

fields.label: Data Protection
fields.hint: Specify requirements for data encryption, storage, and transmission. Example: "All sensitive data must be encrypted at rest and in transit using AES-256 encryption." Example: "Data backups must be stored securely and tested regularly."

fields.label: Monitoring and Logging
fields.hint: Define requirements for system monitoring, logging, and alerting. Example: "All user activity must be logged and retained for 12 months." Example: "Critical security events must trigger alerts within 5 minutes of detection."

fields.label: Vulnerability Management
fields.hint: Outline how vulnerabilities should be identified, assessed, and remediated. Example: "All systems must be scanned for vulnerabilities on a weekly basis." Example: "Critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 48 hours of discovery."

fields.label: Compliance
fields.hint: Specify any regulatory or policy compliance requirements. Example: "The system must comply with GDPR data protection standards." Example: "All security controls must align with the organization's Information Security Policy."

fields.label: Incident Response
fields.hint: Define requirements for incident detection, reporting, and response. Example: "All security incidents must be reported to the Security Operations Center (SOC) within 1 hour." Example: "An incident response plan must be in place and tested annually."

fields.label: Physical Security (if applicable)
